conviction_note: Two-sided non-result: a larger currency tailwind than Q3 points to reported revenue at or above a disputed $1.46-1.51B bar, but this name sold its last revenue beat (Q3 FY26: +$60M revenue beat, EPS short, -0.45%) and EPS looks near or below a disputed $1.22-1.27 bar once FX conversion costs, Chile and new-club costs are counted. The findings net to about 0, p_up is 50, and abs_move stays at about the name's median reaction because the call also previews September comps.

findings.finding: Currency tailwind into FQ4 (Jun-Aug 2026) is larger than in Q3. On the 2026-07-09 call management said June comps were +11.2% reported and +6.5% in constant currency, a 4.7-point FX lift against 3.8 points in Q3. The COP traded about 3,050-3,390 per USD in Jun-Aug 2026 against about 4,030-4,050 in late August 2025, roughly 25% stronger. The CRC traded about 449-454 against about 505 a year earlier. Colombia's Q3 reported net merchandise sales were +35.3% against +18.6% in constant currency. From Q4 FY25 net merchandise sales of $1,302.7M, total revenue lands near $1.49B (+12%). That is above MarketBeat's $1.46B bar (+9.7% implied) and below Benzinga's $1.51B. The same tailwind should carry into the September comps preview the company usually gives on the call (2026-10-27).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-07-08): revenue $1.48B beat consensus by about $60M while EPS $1.28 was reported as short of $1.32 (other sources say ahead of $1.23); the stock moved -0.45%. Q4 FY25 (2025-10-30): EPS $1.02 vs $1.08; -6.48%. Revenue beats have not been paid for on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: A two-source revenue consensus that is $50M apart ($1.46B vs $1.51B) shows the estimate set has not uniformly marked the June-August currency move to market. If it had, both aggregators would sit near $1.49-1.51B. The stock has been flat for 20 days, with no run-up into the print.
findings.independence: COP rates: https://medellin.co/blog/colombian-peso-strongest-decade-dollar-falls-july-2026/ (2026-07-24) and https://medellin.co/blog/colombia-peso-slides-dollar-above-3200-august-28-2026-expats; COP late Aug 2025 about 4,030-4,052: https://www.hsbnoticias.com/?p=231676 (snippet only, single day). CRC: https://observador.cr/cada-dolar-de-hoy-vale-24780-menos-que-en-junio-del-2022/ (2026-08). Q3 FX split: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001041803/000104180326000030/psmt-20260531xexx991.htm. These are different sources pointing the same way, all resting on one fact (stronger local currencies).

findings.finding: EPS is likely near or below the $1.27 bar even with the revenue tailwind. Q3 total other expense rose to a $10.5M net loss from $7.2M on additional FX conversion costs, and $44.1M of cash is trapped in Trinidad. Warehouse operating costs rose to 9.7% of revenue on Chile launch costs. Two clubs added pre-opening cost in the quarter: Ciudad Quesada opened in August and Montego Bay on 2026-10-01. Q4 FY25 base: operating income $52.75M (3.96% of revenue), other expense $5.59M, and a 32.0% tax rate against 27.4% FY26 year to date. At about $1.49B revenue, a 4.0-4.1% operating margin, about $8.5-10M other expense and a 28% tax rate, EPS comes to about $1.18-1.25, below MarketBeat's $1.27 and near Benzinga's $1.22. The tax normalisation is the one offset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS shortfalls: Q4 FY25 $1.02 vs $1.08, -6.48%; Q3 FY26 EPS reported as short of $1.32 on a revenue beat, -0.45%. Q1 FY26 was reported by Benzinga as $1.29 vs $1.44 yet the stock rose 4.55%, so the EPS line is not a reliable driver either.
findings.why_not_priced: The two EPS bars disagree by $0.05 ($1.22 vs $1.27), so the street has not settled how much of the currency tailwind reaches EPS. If the higher bar had been marked down for FX conversion costs and Chile, the sources would agree near $1.20.
findings.independence: Q3 FY26 call transcript (other expense, Chile costs, Trinidad cash): https://s202.q4cdn.com/888601813/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Q3-26-earnings-call-transcript.pdf; Montego Bay opening: https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/news/20261002/pricesmart-opens-mobay-club-us28m-investment. The model is my own arithmetic on company documents.

findings.finding: Colombian consumer demand outside vehicles slowed into the quarter. DANE retail sales were +5.3% real in July 2026 (the slowest since September 2024, below an 11.2% expectation) and +7.3% in August (below 8.5%), but only +1.9% excluding vehicles and motorcycles. PriceSmart's Colombia constant-currency comps were +18.9% in Q3, and Colombia is about 12% of sales, so a cc slowdown there would trim consolidated cc comps by a few tenths.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable. In Q3 Colombia cc comps of +18.9% coincided with a -0.45% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro proxy that no PSMT preview mentions. If it were priced, estimates would show cc comps decelerating, but the constant-currency trend is not visible in any consensus figure. It is a proxy, sized small, net of the 88% of sales outside Colombia (Central America comps +5.2% cc in Q3).
findings.independence: DANE July bulletin: https://www.dane.gov.co/files/operaciones/EMC/bol-EMC-jul2026.pdf; Trading Economics: https://tradingeconomics.com/colombia/retail-sales-annual/news/584275. A broad series, not company-level.
